goal: Adds a coverage_check argument to the deterministic-fuzz-coverage devtool so a developer can run only the per-input check or only the combined check instead of always running both.
Saves time for contributors debugging fuzz coverage nondeterminism, since the combined run can be slow.
reviewability: Ready. Two ACKs (crACK, tACK) after the author addressed prior nits, and the outstanding suggestion from maflcko was a non-blocking style preference.
agreement: Strong. Crypt-iQ and marcofleon gave crACK/tACK after review, and maflcko approved with only a stylistic suggestion (named args over an enum) that was not treated as blocking (maflcko).
jeanpablojp's earlier nit about commit message motivation was addressed by the author (jeanpablojp, HowHsu).

result.summary: This PR adds an optional coverage_check argument (both/single/combined) to the contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage Rust tool, letting a developer run only the per-input check or only the combined check instead of always running both. It updates the README usage text accordingly. The change is purely additive to an existing developer tool used to detect fuzz coverage nondeterminism.
result.problem: Running the full deterministic-fuzz-coverage check (both individual-input and combined-input passes) is time-consuming, and a developer debugging a specific class of nondeterminism (per-input vs. cross-input state leakage) has to wait for both passes even when only one is relevant. The author hit this directly while fixing a coverage issue.

open_concerns: maflcko suggested a simpler design (a bool or named args instead of an enum with positional args) but approved anyway, calling it a possible future cleanup rather than a blocker.
Crypt-iQ left a minor wording nit on the README description of 'both' mode; unclear if implemented before the crACK.
resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp's nit to move the motivation into the commit message was addressed by the author in a later push.
